facts.fact: Net revenues were a record $21.3 billion for the second quarter, compared with $16.8 billion a year ago.
facts.quote: Morgan Stanley (NYSE: MS) today reported net revenues of $21.3 billion for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026 compared with $16.8 billion a year ago.
facts.location: headline and opening paragraph; financial summary table net revenues row; first highlights bullet (record)
common_errors: using six-month net revenues of $41,928 million as the quarter
citing the 4% sequential increase from $20,580 million as the year-over-year change
using total non-interest revenues ($18,568 million) or interest income ($15,902 million) as net revenues
comparing against the non-GAAP 2Q25 net revenues excluding DCP of $16,415 million as if it were the reported prior-year figure

facts.fact: GAAP net income applicable to Morgan Stanley was $5.6 billion, or a record $3.46 per diluted share.
facts.quote: Net income applicable to Morgan Stanley was $5.6 billion, or $3.46 per diluted share, compared with $3.5 billion, or $2.13 per diluted share, for the same period a year ago.
facts.location: headline and opening paragraph; CEO quote ("record EPS of $3.46"); footnote 12 (EPS record qualified as excluding DVA before 2016); financial summary table net income and diluted EPS rows
equivalent_phrasings: compared with $3.5 billion, or $2.13 per diluted share, a year ago
common_errors: reporting basic EPS of $3.50 as diluted
labeling $3.46 as adjusted or non-GAAP (Morgan Stanley reports no adjusted EPS in this release; it is GAAP)
using net income including noncontrolling interests of $5,653 million or earnings applicable to common shareholders of $5,436 million
using six-month diluted EPS of $6.90
using pre-tax income of $7.3 billion as net income

facts.fact: Institutional Securities reported record net revenues of $11.0 billion, compared with $7.6 billion a year ago.
facts.quote: Institutional Securities reported net revenues of $11.0 billion compared with $7.6 billion a year ago.
facts.location: Institutional Securities section opening sentence; highlights bullet (record); segment table net revenues row
common_errors: attributing Investment Banking's 58%, Equity's 69% or Fixed Income's 13% growth to Institutional Securities total net revenues (the release prints no growth rate for the segment total; the derived figure of about 44%, from $11,040 million vs $7,643 million, is accepted)
confusing segment net revenues with segment pre-tax income of $4.3 billion
using the Firm income statement investment banking line ($2,651 million) instead of the segment Investment Banking figure ($2,437 million)

facts.fact: Return on tangible common equity (ROTCE), a non-GAAP measure, was 26.6%, up from 18.2% a year ago.
facts.location: headline; second highlights bullet; financial summary table ROTCE row (footnote 6 defines it as non-GAAP)
equivalent_phrasings: return on average tangible common equity of 26.6%
common_errors: presenting ROTCE as a GAAP measure
confusing ROTCE with GAAP return on equity of 20.7%
using six-month ROTCE of 26.8% or prior-quarter ROTCE of 27.1%
saying ROTCE improved sequentially (it slipped from 27.1% in 1Q26)

facts.fact: Institutional Securities Equity net revenues were a record $6,300 million, up 69% from a year ago.
facts.location: Institutional Securities segment table row; 'Equity net revenues up 69%' subheading and bullet
equivalent_phrasings: Equities drove the quarter, with notable strength in Asia
common_errors: confusing segment Equity net revenues ($6,300 million) with Firm-wide trading revenues ($6,723 million)
swapping the Equity growth rate (69%) with Investment Banking (58%) or Fixed Income (13%)
reading the table in billions instead of millions

facts.fact: Wealth Management delivered record net revenues of $8.9 billion, generating a pre-tax margin of 30.5%.
facts.quote: Wealth Management delivered record net revenues of $8.9 billion on strong asset management fees, robust client activity and higher net interest income, generating a pre-tax margin of 30.5%.
facts.location: highlights bullet; Wealth Management section opening paragraph; segment table net revenues row
common_errors: confusing the Wealth Management pre-tax margin of 30.5% with the Firm pre-tax margin of 34%
citing ex-DCP comparisons, which the Firm no longer presents

facts.fact: Wealth Management added a record $148 billion of net new assets, of which just over half represented inflows related to IPOs of certain Workplace clients.
facts.quote: Strong net new assets for the quarter were $148 billion of which just over half represented inflows related to IPOs of certain clients in our Workplace channel.
facts.location: Wealth Management section opening paragraph; CEO quote (record); financial summary table net new assets row
equivalent_phrasings: roughly half from Workplace IPO inflows
common_errors: presenting the $148 billion as recurring organic flow without the IPO caveat
confusing net new assets with fee-based asset flows of $39.1 billion (which fell from $42.8 billion)
confusing net new assets with fee-based client assets of $3,022 billion or the $10 trillion total client assets milestone

facts.fact: The Board declared a quarterly dividend of $1.15 per share, an increase of 15 cents, payable August 14, 2026.
facts.quote: The Board of Directors declared a $1.15 quarterly dividend per share, an increase of 15 cents, payable on August 14, 2026 to common shareholders of record on July 31, 2026.
common_errors: stating the increase as $1.15 rather than the new level
confusing the payable date (August 14, 2026) with the record date (July 31, 2026)
reporting the dividend as unchanged

facts.fact: The Board reauthorized a multi-year share repurchase program of up to $20 billion, with no set expiration date, beginning in the third quarter of 2026.
facts.quote: The Board of Directors reauthorized a multi-year common equity share repurchase program of up to $20 billion, without a set expiration date, beginning in the third quarter of 2026.
common_errors: confusing the $20 billion authorization with the $1.5 billion repurchased during the second quarter
describing it as an annual program or one with an expiration date
calling it an increase over a prior authorization (the release says reauthorized and gives no prior amount)

facts.fact: The Standardized Common Equity Tier 1 capital ratio was 14.8%, compared with 15.0% a year ago.
facts.quote: The Standardized Common Equity Tier 1 capital ratio was 14.8%.
facts.location: highlights bullet; capital table Standardized Approach CET1 row
common_errors: using the Advanced Approach CET1 ratio of 16.2%
using the Standardized Tier 1 capital ratio of 16.5%
saying the ratio rose year over year (it fell from 15.0%)

traps: GAAP vs non-GAAP: net revenues, net income ($5.6 billion) and diluted EPS ($3.46) are GAAP; ROTCE (26.6%) and tangible book value per share ($53.18) are non-GAAP; there is no adjusted EPS in this release.

Prior-year comparability: 2Q25 net revenues included DCP mark-to-market gains ($294 million in Wealth Management); the 2Q25 ex-DCP figures ($16,415 million net revenues, $6,819 million compensation) are non-GAAP and are no longer presented for 2026. A brief need not carry this caveat; it errs only if it presents ex-DCP comparisons.
Capital ratios (Standardized CET1 14.8%, Tier 1 16.5%) are estimates as of July 15, 2026 and subject to change in the 10-Q (footnote 18); stating 14.8% plainly is correct.

Quarter vs six months: the income statement carries six-month columns ($41,928 million net revenues, $6.90 diluted EPS, 26.8% ROTCE), and the 65% expense efficiency ratio highlight is stated for the first half (the quarter is also 65, versus 71 a year ago).
Year over year vs sequential: the income statement also shows change versus 1Q26 (net revenues up 4% sequentially, 27% year over year); ROTCE actually fell from 27.1% in 1Q26.

Segment vs Firm: segment Investment Banking ($2,437 million) and Equity ($6,300 million) differ from the Firm income statement investment banking ($2,651 million) and trading ($6,723 million) lines; Wealth Management pre-tax margin is 30.5% while the Firm pre-tax margin is 34%.
Units: summary tables are in $ millions except rows labeled ($ billions): fee-based client assets $3,022 billion, AUM $2,004 billion, loans $195.7 billion.
Record claims for Firm pre-tax income, EPS and Institutional Securities revenues are qualified in footnote 12 (excluding DVA in periods before 2016).
The $178 million severance charge was recognized in the first quarter of 2026, not this quarter.
Net new assets of $148 billion were just over half IPO-related Workplace inflows; fee-based asset flows actually fell to $39.1 billion from $42.8 billion.
No guidance or outlook is given; any forward revenue, margin or ROTCE target is invented.
Net income applicable to Morgan Stanley ($5,581 million) differs from net income including noncontrolling interests ($5,653 million); basic EPS is $3.50 and diluted EPS is $3.46.
